summary: Frontend-only verification of the Management 2-tier org-chart change on team.html (Osman Kara promoted above the 3 board members). Tested at 1920px, 1024px and 390px with computed-style + geometry assertions, plus a regression scan of the other 3 departments. All targeted acceptance criteria PASSED. Desktop/tablet: chair node renders above the tier, left-aligned with the tier's left edge (x=465 vs 465 @1920; 61 vs 61 @1024), lead-in trunk (1x26px) above the chair and a down-trunk (1x26px) from the chair bottom into the horizontal spine (spine x=465 -> right=1299, aligning exactly with the last member's dot center), 3 vertical drops via .tm-node::before at each member's dot center, tier members all on the same row. The stray-line bug is FIXED: .tm-node--chair::before computes to display:none on desktop/tablet (no floating fragment), while the generic member ::before is display:block. Mobile (390px, the item flagged as unverified by the main agent) is CORRECT: .tm-network-root and .tm-network-tier both compute display:contents so all 4 members flow into one continuous vertical timeline in order Osman Kara (y=545) -> Omer Kara (616) -> Prof. Dr. Yalcin Sahin (687) -> Gurcan Ayaz (757); the chair's ::before is restored (display:block, 16x1px stub at left:-22px) and its dot (6px at x=21) sits on the same vertical rail as the members' 5px dots (x=21), so there is no visual break, no missing connector and no overlapping text; trunk/spine spans are display:none as intended. Zero horizontal overflow at all 3 breakpoints (scrollWidth == clientWidth: 1920/1920, 1024/1024, 390/390). data-testid team-card-management-1..4 all present with correct name/role text. Regression: Construction & Engineering (3), Architecture & Design (3) and Finance & Legal (4) remain unchanged single-row networks (same-row true, spines terminating on the last dot center, 4-col spine correctly widening to right=1342). Hover interaction still works (name transitions to bronze rgb(154,130,83)). Zero JS console errors and zero page errors across all runs.

issues: Pre-existing/consistent (not a regression): the horizontal spine starts at the container's far-left edge (x=465) while the first vertical drop is ~40px inward (x=505 for the single-row depts, x=620 for the Management tier), leaving a short dangling spine segment on the left. For Management this reads correctly as the chair's trunk feed-in, but for the 3 single-row departments it reads as a small orphan line stub. Cosmetic only - flagging for the designer's judgement, no action strictly required.

critical_code_review_comments: CSS specificity around .tm-network--rooted is fragile-but-currently-correct: `.tm-network--rooted { padding-top: 0 }` (line 173) and the `@media (max-width:900px) .tm-network { padding-top: 6px; padding-left: 22px }` (line 203) have equal specificity, so the mobile rule only wins because it is declared later in the file. Verified live (rooted network computes padding-top:6px / padding-left:22px at 390px), but any future reordering of team.css would silently break the mobile Management timeline. Consider hoisting the rooted rules above the media queries explicitly or scoping the mobile override with `.tm-network, .tm-network--rooted`.
seed_data_creation: None - static frontend, no data required.
context_for_next_testing_agent: team.html Management department now uses .tm-network--rooted with .tm-network-root (Osman Kara, .tm-node--chair) + .tm-network-tier (3 board members). Verified fully at 1920/1024/390 in iteration_14: hierarchy, connectors, chair stray-line fix, mobile display:contents timeline, zero overflow, zero console errors. Other 3 departments unchanged. Useful assertions if re-testing: .tm-node--chair ::before must be display:none <=1100px+ and display:block <=900px; .tm-network-root/.tm-network-tier must compute display:contents at <=900px; tier spine right edge must equal last node's dot center. partners.html (iteration_12) is unrelated and untouched.
rca_of_the_issue: Not applicable - no defects found. The previously reported stray line fragment near Osman Kara was caused by the generic `.tm-node::before` vertical connector stub (left:50%; top:-26px) still rendering for the chair node, which has no parent above it; the fix (`.tm-node--chair::before { display:none }` on desktop, re-enabled as display:block inside the max-width:900px media query for the mobile timeline stub) is confirmed effective at all three breakpoints.
